Saudi cities faced the threat of a second day of Houthi attacks as fighting across Yemen led the UN to warn of a humanitarian crisis with 100,000 Yemenis already displaced.

As oil prices remained well over $100 (£74) a barrel, Qatar warned of a catastrophe if the Iran-backed Houthi militants won full control of the Bab al-Mandab strait, the narrow waterway at the bottom of the Red Sea dominating the key naval route to Asia. The strait has become vital to Saudi crude oil exports as the wider Middle East war chokes the strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.

Continue reading...

events.title: ‘This should be condemned by any thinking human’: film industry rallies behind NAZA directors
events.summary:
Backing comes after Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor were threatened with having their citizenship revoked and accused of treason

Film industry heavyweights across the globe have expressed solidarity with Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, the Oscar-winning Israeli directors of documentary NAZA, who have been threatened with having their citizenship revoked by Israel’s culture minister, who accused them of “treason against the state”.

NAZA, which was produced by the Guardian, is named for an acronym euphemistically used by Israel’s intelligence service to indicate how many civilians it expects to die in an airstrike on Gaza. It includes interviews with 24 Israeli military or intelligence soldiers and officers who outlined the AI-powered targeting systems used to bombard Gaza, resulting in the mass killing of Palestinian civilians.

Continue reading...

events.title: UK sanctions on Israel ‘fall far short’ of its obligations, legal experts say
events.summary:
More than 130 sign letter to PM saying international law requires further measures to stop illegal settlements

More than 130 legal experts, including 18 king’s counsel (KCs), have written to Andy Burnham saying that sanctions on Israeli settlements “fall far short” of Britain’s obligations under the international court of justice’s (ICJ’s) finding that the occupation is unlawful.

The foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, last week announced an import ban on goods from illegal Israeli settlements in Palestine and other measures. Signatories to the letter to the prime minister, including the leading lawyers Michael Mansfield KC and Imran Khan KC, and the former lord justice of appeal Alan Moses, say it is not enough.

Continue reading...

events.title: Houthis seize strategic Red Sea islands as analysts warn of impending oil crunch
events.summary:
The militant group in Yemen captured the islands of Greater and Lesser Hanish, near the chokepoint of the Bab al-Mandab strait

Yemen’s Houthi militants have seized two strategic islands in the Red Sea, reinforcing the Iran-backed group’s ability to control a key shipping route, as concerns mount that the world is facing a new oil supply crisis.

The seizure of the islands of Greater and Lesser Hanish is the latest in the militant group’s swift advance across Yemen’s Red Sea coast, after the capture of the port of Mokha and Perim island in the Bab al-Mandab strait.

Continue reading...

events.title: US borrowing costs hit 5% for first time since 2023 amid bond sell-off
events.summary:
Soaring oil prices of above $108 a barrel after Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure stoke inflation fears

US government borrowing costs have risen to 5% for the first time since 2023 as soaring oil prices fuelled by the war in the Middle East trigger an intensifying sell-off in the global bond market.

The yield – in effect the interest rate – on 10-year US Treasury bonds hit the psychologically important threshold on Monday, on a day of renewed selling pressure on Wall Street as the global oil price reached $108 a barrel.

Continue reading...

events.title: Imran Khan’s sons accuse Pakistani army chief of vendetta against imprisoned father
events.summary:
Kasim and Sulaiman Khan tell Guardian they believe ex-PM is being ‘slowly killed’ by harsh treatment, driven by Asim Munir

The sons of Imran Khan have accused Pakistan’s powerful army chief of a “personal vendetta” against the incarcerated former prime minister and expressed fears their father is being “slowly killed” in jail, as international pressure mounts over his prison conditions.

Kasim Khan, 27, and Sulaiman Khan, 29, have become strong advocates for the release of their father, who has been held in Adiala prison in Rawalpindi since his arrest in 2023, and is serving a 14-year sentence on corruption charges.

Continue reading...

events.title: What would it take to make India’s cities better – and safer?
events.summary:
After a five-storey building collapsed in Delhi, focus is on how urban areas can adapt to growing populations. Plus, Ahmedabad’s ace newspaper delivery driver goes viral

• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

Recently, I may have saved a woman’s life on the road. Somehow, this was something I had expected to happen.

On that day, I saw a truck leave a construction site with a tangled wire trailing behind. I frantically looked to see what the wire was attached to and spotted the scaffolding a few meters ahead. I shrieked and grabbed the hand of the woman walking in front of me just as the metal pipes came crashing down. We hugged for a brief second, and then walked our separate ways.

events.title: CIA releases dozens of presidential daily briefs on Bin Laden and al-Qaida from before 9/11
events.summary:
The presidential briefing documents were declassified on the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks

Several dozen presidential briefing documents declassified on Friday, the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, detail intelligence that government officials had gathered about Osama bin Laden and al-Qaida leading up to the hijackings that killed nearly 3,000 people and upended American national security.

The documents illustrate security analysts’ tracking of Bin Laden’s movements and support system, as well as concerns about possible threats to US targets. They also detail officials’ understanding of his network in the United States and other countries, including how his operations were financed.

Continue reading...

events.title: ‘Our forefathers are coming back’: Naga people celebrate after Oxford museum agrees to return remains
events.summary:
Following six years of talks, Pitt Rivers Museum will return body parts collected by British colonial administrators to north-east India

Anthropologists and community leaders from Nagaland, a remote state in north-eastern India bordering Myanmar, have expressed joy and relief that human remains belonging to their ancestors that had been on display in a British museum for nearly a century are finally being returned.

On Monday, the Pitt Rivers Museum in Oxford announced that 39 pieces of human remains – including parts of skulls, a finger and a piece of skin with hair – belonging to the Naga tribes, will be returned to Nagaland after six years of negotiation between the community and the museum.

Continue reading...

events.title: ‘Trust deficit’: Why India’s economic data has sparked a furore
events.summary:
India’s statistical system once commanded respect, and its data on economic and social indicators was considered rigorous – that appears to have eroded

• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

There isn’t much that we Indians agree on these days. GDP numbers are no exception. Last week, India released glowing GDP numbers for the latest quarter – 7.8% growth – higher than the forecast 7%. It sparked a furore.

Subhash Garg, a former finance secretary under Narendra Modi’s government and now a critic, reframed what Modi called a “herculean feat” as mere smoke and mirrors. According to Garg, the government revised last year’s current-price GDP downwards to inflate this year’s number – he believes the real growth is only 2.6%.

Continue reading...

events.title: British bosses to be forced to meet with employees who request flexible working
events.summary:
Employers will have to hold face-to-face meetings with staff who ask about shift changes under government reforms

Company bosses will have to sit down with workers who request flexible working and justify their reasons for any refusals under new rights announced by Louise Haigh on Tuesday.

The first secretary of state told the TUC conference that employers would have to “properly consider” requests for flexibility and offer a face-to-face meeting under new rights for workers.

Continue reading...

events.title: People from ethnic groups feel racial equality is worsening, UK study shows
events.summary:
Nearly half of ethnic minority respondents in a poll say they have faced prejudice over the past year

Many Britons feel inequality is worsening and that discrimination has become more common, according to a thinktank study.

The report by British Future has found that people across ethnic groups believe racial equality is worsening in Britain. One in six people are from ethnic minority backgrounds.

Continue reading...

events.title: Thirlwall inquiry has left biggest questions around the Letby case unanswered
events.summary:
Decision not to pause proceedings means £18m report does not engage with concerns over former nurse’s conviction

Just two months before Lady Justice Kathryn Thirlwall opened her inquiry into events at the Countess of Chester hospital and the crimes of Lucy Letby, a report by Chris Henley KC was published into the “atrocious” wrongful conviction of Andrew Malkinson for rape.

Henley prefaced that report with a plea for the legal establishment to recognise that the criminal courts produce miscarriages of justice. Right up to top judges in the court of appeal, Henley wrote, the system has “a deep-seated … cultural reluctance” to accept it “will on occasion make mistakes” and that “entirely innocent defendants will sometimes be convicted”.

Continue reading...

events.title: UK paying £56,000 for each person returned to France under ‘one in one out’ scheme
events.summary:
Home secretary defends cost, saying it is about the same or cheaper than putting someone up in a hotel for a year

The government’s “one in, one out” deal is costing about £56,000 for every person sent back to France, Shabana Mahmood has told MPs.

The home secretary disclosed the figure as she was questioned by the home affairs select committee over whether the scheme was delivering value for taxpayers.

events.title: Leader of Reform UK in Wales stands down after arrest on suspicion of assault
events.summary:
Dan Thomas, elected in May, says he does not wish to be a ‘distraction’ on same day Reform MS defects to Plaid Cymru

The leader of Reform UK in Wales is standing down after he was arrested and bailed on suspicion of assault and controlling or coercive behaviour.

Dan Thomas, a former Tory councillor, had only been announced as Reform’s Welsh leader by Nigel Farage in February.

events.title: Blanche defends Trump’s tirade against supreme court after it blocked mail-in voting executive order – US politics live
events.summary:
Attorney general says president ‘should communicate his concerns with the supreme court’ after Trump said justices ‘really let our country down’

  • Sign up for US Breaking News emails

Kash Patel, the FBI director, is now testifying before lawmakers on the Senate judiciary committee. A reminder that the last time he appeared before Congress was in May, when he sparred with senators on the appropriations committee and denied – under oath – allegations of excessive drinking and unexplained absences on the job, dismissing them as “baseless” during a fiery congressional hearing.

Today’s hearing is also expected to be full of heated exchanges. “Mr Patel is the least qualified and most partisan FBI director in our nation’s history,” said Senator Dick Durbin, the judiciary committee’s top Democrat. “The bureau has been reshaped as a political weapon against President Trump’s political enemies and a shield to protect the president and his MAGA loyalists, not the American people.”

events.title: Ed Sheeran responds to backlash over removing Macklemore from tour after ‘Free Palestine’ comments
events.summary:
English singer outlines his position after US stadium owners refuse to let rapper perform after political speech

  • Macklemore dropped from Ed Sheeran’s US tour after ‘free Palestine’ speech

Singer Ed Sheeran has responded to the backlash over the removal of Macklemore from his North American Loop tour, following the rapper’s “Free Palestine” speech on stage at MetLife stadium in New Jersey.

In a two-minute speech on 4 September, the Grammy-winning artist told the audience he wanted the people of Gaza and “the occupied West Bank” to know “we have not forgotten about them”, prompting owners of subsequent stadium tour venues – including Robert Kraft, the billionaire owner of the New England Patriots and a prominent supporter of and donor to Israel – to object to Macklemore’s appearance on the tour.

Continue reading...

events.title: Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon call for curbs on AI at ‘pro-human’ summit
events.summary:
Leftwing senator and far-right strategist rail against tech oligarchs but offer competing visions on Chinese ‘cold war’

The progressive senator Bernie Sanders and rightwing strategist Steve Bannon have called for restrictions on artificial intelligence (AI) but offered competing visions for what they termed a “cold war” with China.

Speaking at the “Pro-Human Assembly” in Washington on Tuesday, the ideological adversaries were united in warning of the potential dangers of AI and demanding stringent guardrails against Silicon Valley’s “oligarchs”.

events.title: Man admits to bombing California courthouse in retaliation for seized guns
events.summary:
Nathaniel James McGuire faces maximum sentence of life in prison after guilty plea over September 2024 bombing

A California man has pleaded guilty to charges that he detonated a bomb at a Santa Maria courthouse in 2024 in retaliation for law enforcement officers seizing his firearms earlier that year.

In September 2024, Nathaniel James McGuire, 22, of Santa Barbara county threw a backpack containing an explosive device into the courthouse before exiting the building to retrieve two long guns and 10 molotov cocktails from his car.

events.title: Fourth person dies of measles-associated illness in US
events.summary:
All deaths occurred in Pennsylvania, in worst year since 1992 for one of the most contagious diseases

Pennsylvania health officials said a fourth person had died of measles-associated illness in the worst year for the disease since 1992. All four US deaths have occurred in the state.

Due to the Trump administration changing how it reports measles deaths, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) does not count any of the deaths in its national tally. Three people died in 2025.

events.title: With a performance defined by emotion, Céline Dion brings her story to Paris
events.summary: Céline Dion on Saturday fulfilled her dream of returning to the stage after years battling a rare neurological disorder with a sell-out concert in an arena west of Paris. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Mark Owen, vocal coach Elena Hurstel says that Céline Dion's performance in Paris has been defined by emotion, explaining that "we can really see the new Céline. It's not about being perfect, it's about being the woman she became, about being real".

events.title: Viral Putin, Modi and Xi selfie at BRICS summit is AI-generated

A SynthID watermark shows it was created using OpenAI tools, while several leaders pictured, including Brazil’s Lula and Turkey’s Erdogan, did not attend. Another AI selfie features former Iranian president Ebrahim Raisi, who died in 2024. Both images were widely shared online, including by official embassy accounts. Vedika Bahl fact-checks.

events.title: Analysts call for step-up in response to Russia after Denmark, Lithuania incidents

events.title: 'Revolutionary change in American foreign policy': Canada pivoting towards EU, India and China
events.summary: François Picard is pleased to welcome Anne Applebaum, staff writer at The Atlantic and author of Autocracy, Inc. According to Applebaum, the upheaval in American diplomacy and foreign policy transcends any one administration. She describes a full-fledged transformation in the way the United States exerts power, pivoting away from leadership of a democratic alliance and toward a transactional, mafia-style politics that fuses ideology, private economic interests, personal relationships and geopolitical leverage.

events.title: Canada's Carney seeks closer Europe ties to counter hostile US

FRANCE 24's Christopher Guly reports from Ottawa.

events.title: Saudi crown prince seeks neighbours' backing as Houthi attacks rattle Red Sea oil routes

The two regional powers discussed the threat posed by the Iran-backed group's control over the Bab al-Mandab Strait. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell has more.

events.title: US acknowledges for the first time that it has deployed weapons in space

events.title: Rapid data center expansion incites backlash in Republican stronghold

Pierrick Leurent and Valérie Defert have this report.

events.title: Amid France’s political 'fragmentation', 'a case needs to be made for participatory democracy’
events.summary: Carys Garland is pleased to welcome Dr. Andrew Smith, Historian of Modern France and Lecturer in Liberal Arts at Queen Mary University of London. He argues that Marine Le Pen and the National Rally’s commanding position in early presidential polling should not be regarded as an inevitable far-right victory. They are benefiting from familiarity, unity and laser-focused messaging. More fundamentally, however, Smith sees the polling as a reflection of a French electorate shaped by anger, anxiety, economic insecurity and political fatigue. Rather than describing this landscape simply as one of growing “polarization,” he proposes the more revealing concept of “fragmentation.”

events.title: Corruption ‘endemic’ in Trump administration: 'Checks and balances only in effect at lower courts'
events.summary: François Picard is pleased to welcome Andrew Weissmann, Author, Professor at NYU School of Law, and former General Counsel of the FBI. He argues that as political deception and deliberate falsehoods become normalized, and politically useful, it erodes any trust we have in our government and our institutions. Drawing on his book, "Liar’s Kingdom", Weissmann questions why political leaders are above the law in the United States, while ordinary citizens risk serious legal consequences for making intentionally false statements.

events.title: Lack of 'enforcement of EU laws': Consumer products contain 'illegal levels of restricted chemicals'
events.summary: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Hélène Duguy, Senior Environmental Lawyer at ClientEarth. PFAS pollution is widespread, these highly persistent chemicals have been detected in water and soil, food and consumer products, and even the human body. The risks are increasingly well documented, alternatives now exist for many uses, and there is an extensive regulatory framework that is in place. Duguy argues that the central problem is therefore not simply a lack of scientific knowledge or legislation, but rather weak enforcement, slow regulation and corporate resistance. And so hazardous chemicals remain in circulation even when restrictions exist.

events.title: Russia and Ukraine launch new energy attacks despite Trump’s ceasefire claim
events.summary: President Donald Trump said Russia and Ukraine had agreed to stop striking each other’s energy infrastructure.

events.title: U.S. and China face grave AI risks but mutual distrust stalls cooperation
events.summary: The United States and China are both gripped by safety fears as they reckon with their rapid advances in AI, but intensifying competition and deep mutual distrust could derail the kind of cooperation experts say is vital to head off the strategically vital technology’s greatest dangers.

events.title: Graphic: Tracking ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz
events.summary: Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has been at a near-standstill for weeks amid the Iran war, sending prices of oil and other key goods soaring.

events.title: Tracking U.S., state and county gas prices, in maps and charts
events.summary: Are gas prices declining? NBC News is tracking national, state and county prices at the pump.

events.title: Air Force officer recalls ‘free-falling’ after jet was shot down over Iran
events.summary: In an interview with CBS’ “60 Minutes,” one of the two U.S. Air Force officers whose fighter jet was shot down over Iran in April detailed his harrowing ordeal.

events.title: Israeli directors talk about controversial ‘NAZA’ documentary
events.summary: 'NAZA,' which won the Special Jury Prize at the Venice Film Festival, uses testimony from Israeli military insiders to document the purported systematic killing of civilians in Gaza.

events.title: Chinese company releases video of humanoid robot walking off assembly line on its own
events.summary: Chinese company Xpeng released a video showing its new humanoid robot IRON walking off the assembly line on its own. It’s the latest step in the robot arms race between the U.S. and China that could eventually lead to mass production of the humanoids. NBC News’ Priscilla Thompson reports.

events.title: Iran-backed Houthis take control of Red Sea coastline in Yemen
events.summary: The Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen have taken control of a strategic Red Sea coastline, further complicating shipping routes in the region. At the same time, strikes inside Saudi Arabia forced the shutdown of a critical oil pipeline, the country’s energy ministry confirmed.

events.title: Rick Springfield opens up about killing a man in Vietnam while performing for troops in 1968
events.summary: Rocker Rick Springfield recalled how, as a teenager, when he performed for U.S. forces in Vietnam, they came under attack and he killed a Viet Cong — haunting him to this day that he “was responsible for the end of a life.” NBC News' Maggie Vespa reports.

events.title: Harry and Meghan change their children’s school over security concerns
events.summary: Archie and Lilibet, the children of Harry and Meghan, have changed school just days after starting, following security concerns about transporting them.

events.title: How Ukraine’s futuristic war could get ‘much worse,’ according to ex-Google CEO
events.summary: “The rate of innovation is faster than I’ve ever seen, and I work in tech,” Eric Schmidt told NBC News’ Richard Engel.

events.title: 10-year Treasury yield tops 5% as oil surges and diesel hits all-time high
events.summary: Talks between Iran and Gulf countries about the future of the Strait of Hormuz were delayed after a key Saudi pipeline was hit.

events.title: China dismisses AI slowdown calls and blasts ‘fearmongering’ from U.S. tech leaders
events.summary: Urgent calls for a slowdown in the development of artificial intelligence may cite a grave threat to humanity, but China says the warnings are instead aimed at slowing its progress as America’s rival superpower.

events.title: Saudi shutdown of key pipeline limits oil flow as Yemen hits back against Houthis
events.summary: Saudi Arabia has closed a critical oil pipeline after it was struck by drones launched from Iraq, with the latest squeeze reverberating through the region Saturday as attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels threatened to deepen the world’s energy crisis.

events.title: Strikes shut down key Saudi pipeline as Iran-backed Houthis tighten grip on crucial shipping lane
events.summary: Houthi rebels effectively completed a rapid push to take control of Yemen’s Red Sea coastline on Friday, tightening their grip on one of the world’s most important shipping routes and delivering a dramatic boost to their backers in Iran.

events.title: Emma Bonino, leader of abortion and divorce battles that changed Italy, dies at 78
events.summary: Emma Bonino, who rose to political prominence as a leader of campaigns by the Radical Party that legalized abortion and divorce in the 1970s in heavily Roman Catholic Italy, against the objections of the Vatican, has died.

events.title: They led vigils for victims of Tiananmen. Now they’re facing time in prison for it.
events.summary: Three pro-democracy activists in Hong Kong who organized annual vigils for victims of China’s 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown were sentenced Friday under a national security law that critics say has stifled dissent.

events.title: Flight carrying Zelenskyy to Norway was delayed in Moldova because of drone incursion
events.summary: Moldova had closed its airspace to protect planes flying over the country, delaying three departures, including Zelenskyy’s.

events.title: Oil surges past $101 to highest closing level since May as Iran conflict intensifies
events.summary: The price of oil breached the $100 threshold as new flare-ups between the U.S. and Iran stoked fresh concern for global energy markets.

events.title: China hits back at U.S. claim its AI companies systematically copied American models
events.summary: In its most detailed accusation yet, the U.S. government has named six Chinese AI companies that it says copied American companies for their AI secrets.

events.title: Iran attacks American warships and base after U.S. sinks five Iranian tankers
events.summary: They’re the latest tit-for-tat strikes as Washington and Tehran lurch back toward fighting during more than six months of war.
